newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends weaker despite intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends weaker despite intervention.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Monday as a central bank's dollar selling intervention failed to satisfy hungry dollar buyers, dealers said.
But the Bank of Korea denied stepping in, as it routinely does.
The won finished at 844.70 after opening at an intraday high of 843.50. It hit the bottom of 844.80.
The Bank of Korea stepped in in the afternoon at 844.50, trying to cool the won's decline, dealers said.
However, an expected slowdown in exports due to labour strikes coupled with a firmer dollar versus the Japanese yen continued to plague the local currency.
"The central bank's intervention was weaker than expected," said one local trader. "So it failed to cap the dollar's rise."
Dealers said much of Tuesday's trading would depend on the size of year-end export deals and expectation of import settlements at the beginning of the year.
They expected a trading range of 843.50 to 845.50 for Tuesday. -- Jean Yoon (822) 727 5643
